rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Transmitted interpretation identifies the outward sin as adultery and the inward sin as illicit lovers or companions.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن ظاهره الزنا، وباطنه اتخاذ الأخدان والأصدقاء على جهة الريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to leave sin whether openly or secretly, avoiding what God forbids in either state.
rows.anchor: أي لا تقربوا ما حرم الله عليكم جهرا ولا سرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited food is that whose slaughter was not devoted solely to God.
rows.anchor: أي مما لم يخلص ذبحه لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fisq means departure from truth and religion; the date is said to fisq when it comes out of its skin.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الفسق الخروج عن الحق والدين، يقال فسقت الرطبة، إذا خرجت عن قشرتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devils whisper false arguments into their allies' hearts, referring to the polytheists' dispute with Muslims over carrion.
rows.anchor: أي يوسوس الشيطان لوليه فيلقي في قلبه الجدال بالباطل، وهو ما وصفنا من أن المشركين جادلوا المسلمين في الميتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse proves that declaring forbidden what God permits, or permitted what God forbids, makes one a polytheist.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية فيها دليل أن كل من أحل شيئا مما حرم الله عليه أوحرم شيئا مما أحل الله له فهو مشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making carrion lawful outside necessity or making adultery lawful is agreed by the community to be polytheism, even if one obeys God in other commands.
rows.anchor: لو أحل محل الميتة في غير اضطرار، أو أحل الزنا لكان مشركا بإجماع الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a person is called a polytheist because he follows someone besides God and associates that other with God.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي مشركا لأنه اتبع غير الله، فأشرك بالله غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward for good deeds is multiplied from tenfold up to seven hundredfold and beyond.
rows.anchor: ويضاعف الله ذلك بما بين عشرة أضعاف إلى سبعمائة ضعف إلى أضعاف كثيرة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators agree that the evil deed meant here is associating a partner with God.
rows.anchor: وأجمع المفسرون على قوله: (ومن جاء بالسيئة فلا يجزى إلا مثلها)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They identify the good deed as saying There is no god but God; monotheism is the root of good deeds and disbelief the worst sin.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: (من جاء بالحسنة) هي قول لا إله إلا الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the religion that leads to the true religion.
rows.anchor: والصراط الدين الذي دلني على الذين الذي هو دين الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiyaman means upright; qayim is a verbal noun like ṣighar and kibar, with its form affected by the weak verb qāma.
rows.anchor: وقيم مصدر كالصغر والكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form is qayim rather than qawm because the verb qāma became weak; ḥawl, by contrast, is not derived from a verb.
rows.anchor: لأن قولك قام قيما كأنه على قوم أو قوم، فلما اعتل فصار قام اعتل قيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative dīnan qayiman and millata ibrāhīma is semantic: guidance to a straight path implies making him know an upright religion.
rows.anchor: فمحمول على المعنى، لأنه لما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, dīnan qayiman is an apposition to the meaning of guidance to a straight path.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون على البدل من معنى هداني إلى صراط مستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Millata Ibrāhīm is appositional to dīnan qayiman, while ḥanīfan is an accusative circumstantial from Ibrāhīm.
rows.anchor: على الحال من إبراهيم، المعنى هداني وعرفني ملة إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God guided him to Abraham's way while Abraham was a ḥanīf; this description suits Abraham especially well.
rows.anchor: المعنى هداني وعرفني ملة إبراهيم في حال حنيفيته، وهو ههنا لإبراهيم حسن منه لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanīfiyya is inclination toward Islam with no return from it.
rows.anchor: وقد فسرنا معنى الحنيفية وأنها الميل إلى الإسلام ميلا لا رجوع معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis's answer is not grammatically a direct answer: I am better than him implies that his superiority kept him from prostrating; the wording also conveys his present state.
rows.anchor: ولفظه غير جواب، لأن قوله: (أنا خير منه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis asked to be delayed until Resurrection, but was not granted respite until that exact day; he was deferred to the appointed time.
rows.anchor: فلم يجب إلى الإنظار إلى يوم البعث بعينه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation of aghwaytanī is that God led Iblis astray.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: فبما أضللتني

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God called Iblis to something through which he went astray, namely because of Adam.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: فبما دعوتني إلى شيء غويت به

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Grammarians agree that the preposition ʿalā is omitted from the phrase about sitting on God's path; Zajjaj illustrates the omission with striking the back and belly.
rows.anchor: ولا اختلاف بين النحويين في أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leaves them in their punishment just as they neglected to work for the meeting of this Day.
rows.anchor: أي نتركهم في عذابهم كما تركوا العمل للقاء يومهم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause means their denial of God's signs; mā is coordinated with kamā and is in the genitive position.
rows.anchor: نسق على " كما، في موضع جر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the accusative parsing, hudan describes the detailed Book as guidance and as possessing mercy.
rows.anchor: هدى في موضع نصب، أي فصلناه هاديا وذا رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, hudan wa-raḥmatan begins a new sentence: the Book is guidance and mercy for believers.
rows.anchor: على الاستئناف، المعنى هو هدى ورحمة لقوم يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The awaited taʾwīl is what their affair will lead to, namely the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: معناه هل ينظرون إلا ما يؤول إليه أمرهم من البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taʾwīl whose timing only God knows is when the Resurrection will occur; those firmly rooted in knowledge affirm it as Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي ما يعلم متى يكون البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word has readings with nūn bearing ḍamma or fatḥa; ʿĀṣim reads bushrā with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: و (نشرا) أيضا بضم النون وفتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the nushuran reading, the phrase means that God spreads out the winds.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي ينشر الرياح منشرة نشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nushuran can also be a plural of nushūr or nashr.
rows.anchor: ومن قال نشرا فهو جمع نشور ونشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bushran is a plural of bashīra or bashr, as in this verse's description of the winds.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بشرا فهو جمع بشيرة وبشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between God's mercy means before the rain, which is itself mercy.
rows.anchor: أي بين يدي المطر الذي هو رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind is the implied subject of carrying the clouds; aqalla means to carry something.
rows.anchor: حتى إذا أقلت الريح سحابا، يقال: أقل فلان الشيء إذا هو حمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds is the plural of cloud, and thiqālan means heavy with water.
rows.anchor: والسحاب جمع سحابة. (ثقالا) أي ثقالا بالماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two forms may both describe barren land as dead.
rows.anchor: سقناه لبلد ميت). وميت جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows water to be sent down by the cloud, but prefers that the fruit be brought forth by the water; it could also be by the land, since no one land is singled out.
rows.anchor: الأحسن - والله أعلم - فأخرجنا بالماء من كل الثمرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection of the dead is like the preceding bringing forth of fruit.
rows.anchor: أي مثل ذلك الإخراج الذي أشرنا إليه نخرج الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿalla expresses expectation; people are addressed according to their knowledge and what one person hopes from another, while God knows whether they will remember.
rows.anchor: لعل ترج، وإنما خوطب العباد على قدر علمهم، وما يرجوه بعضهم من بعض، والله يعلم أي تذكرون أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are presented so that people infer God's oneness and His resurrection of the dead.
rows.anchor: أي لعلكم بما بيناه لكم تستدلون على توحيد الله وأنه يبعث الموتى

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: The people of Medina read nakdan with fatḥa on the kāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأها أهل المدينة نكدا - بفتح الكاف -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two other linguistic forms are possible, but the form with ḍamma is not recited because no Qurʾanic transmission establishes it.
rows.anchor: ولا يقرأ بالمضمومة، لأنه لم تثبت به رواية في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ means the leaders and notables.
rows.anchor: وهم الرؤساء والأشراف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret al-malaʾ as the men.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم يعنى به الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression describes regret over what was done; both saqaṭa fī yadihi and asqaṭa are used, and a recitation with saquṭa was transmitted.
rows.anchor: قد سقط في يده وأسقط، وقد رويت سقط في القراءة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom pictures regret as falling into one's hands, likening what happens in the heart and soul to something visible.
rows.anchor: تشبه ما يحصل في القلب وفي النفس بما يرى بالعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghaḍbāna is an accusative circumstantial, on the faʿlān pattern with feminine faʿlā, and is diptote because of its alif and nūn, like ḥamrāʾ.
rows.anchor: منصوب على الحال، وهو على مثال فعلان، وله فعلى نحو غضبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asaf means intense anger; 43:55 uses āsafūnā to mean they angered Us.
rows.anchor: الشديد الغضب، قال الله جل وعز: (فلما آسفونا انتقمنا منهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjila al-amra means to get ahead of or precede an affair, while aʿjala means to urge it on.
rows.anchor: يقال عجلت الأمر والشيء سبقته، وأعجلته استحثثته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative is read ibn umm with fatḥa or ibn umm with kasra.
rows.anchor: بالفتح وإن شئت بن أم بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa reflects frequent use of ibn umm and ibn ʿamm; in vocative speech the two words are treated as one compound, like fifteen.
rows.anchor: فجعلوا " ابن " و " أم " شيئا واحدا نحو خمسة عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, the phrase is annexed to the speaker after first being treated as a single name.
rows.anchor: فإنه أضافه إلى نفسه بعد أن جعله اسما واحدا

rows.speaker: العرب
rows.claim: Some Arabs retain the yāʾ and say yā ibn ummī.
rows.anchor: يقول: يا ابن أمي بإثبات الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj cites the unnamed poet's line as evidence for the yā ibn ummī vocative.
rows.anchor: يا ابن أمي ويا شسقيق نفسي. . .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who took the calf made it a god.
rows.anchor: المعنى اتخذوا العجل إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their humiliation followed their recognition that they had gone astray; it was the command that they kill themselves.
rows.anchor: لحقتهم الذلة أنهم رأوا أنهم قد ضلوا وذلوا، والذلة هو ما أمروا به من قتل أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some glossed the humiliation as jizya, but Zajjaj rejects this because the calf worshippers were pardoned through killing themselves instead.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن الذلة أخذ الجزية، وأخذ الجزية لم يقع في الذين عبدوا العجل، لأن الله جل وعز تاب عليهم بقتلهم أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakata can mean became still; sakata can also mean stopped speaking.
rows.anchor: يقال سكت يسكت سكتا إدا هو سكن، وسكت يسكت سكوتا وسكتا إذا قطع الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sukayt describes someone who is often silent; sukāt is an illness that prevents speech; al-sukayt is the last horse to finish, with light or doubled tāʾ.
rows.anchor: ويقال: رجل سكيت بين السكوت والساكوتة إذا كان كثير السكوت، وأصاب فلانا سكات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sukayt, whether with light or doubled tāʾ, is the horse that comes last.
rows.anchor: والسكيت - بالتخفيف والتشديد - الذي يجيء آخر الخيل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some transmitted a reading that makes Moses the one who stopped being angry, but Zajjaj rejects it as contrary to the muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: وروى بعضهم: " ولما سكت عن موسى الغضب " ولا تقرأن به لأنه خلاف المصحف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some explain the wording by inversion: Moses stopped being angry, as when someone says he put the cap into his head.
rows.anchor: معناه: ولما سكت موسى عن الغضب، على القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inversion analogy is putting a cap into one's head, meaning that one put one's head into the cap.
rows.anchor: كما قالوا: أدخلت القلنسوة في رأسي

rows.speaker: أهل العربية
rows.claim: The Arab grammarians' preferred explanation is that the anger became still.
rows.anchor: والقول الذي معناه سكن قول أهل العربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses selected six men from each of twelve tribes, totaling seventy-two, then reduced the group by two.
rows.anchor: فبلغوا اثنين وسبعين رجلا فخفف منهم رجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iḫtāra qawmahu means iḫtāra min qawmihi: the preposition min is omitted and the verb takes a direct object.
rows.anchor: اختار من قومه فحذفت " من " ووصل الفعل فنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic permits both choosing from among the men and taking a direct object after the verb.
rows.anchor: يقال اخترت من الرجال زيد واخترت الرجال زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj cites an unnamed poet's phrase iḫtāra al-rijāla to support the construction without min.
rows.anchor: ومنا الذي اختار الرجال سماحة. . .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-rajfa is intense movement or a severe earthquake.
rows.anchor: وهي الحركة الشديدة والزلزلة الشديدة

rows.speaker: يقال
rows.claim: A report says the mountain shook them and they died.
rows.anchor: يقال إنه رجف بهم الجبل فماتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses means that God could have killed them before bringing on the event that required the quake.
rows.anchor: أي لو شئت أمتهم من قبل أن تأتيهم بما أوجب عليهم الرجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudnā ilayka means we repent to You.
rows.anchor: إنا هدنا إليك). معناه تبنا إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything created lives through God's mercy and bounty; here the verse means that His mercy encompasses everything in this world.
rows.anchor: أي كل ما خلقته فبرحمتي وفضلي يعيش، فمعناه ورحمتي وسعت كل شيء في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God writes this mercy for them in the afterlife by rewarding them there.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة، أي أجازيهم بها في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ummī is on the original nature of the community: he did not learn scripture and remained in his innate state.
rows.anchor: الأمي: هو على خلقة الأمة، لم يتعلم الكتاب فهو على جبلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal particle idh is accusative as the object of a command to remember the time God took the descendants of Adam.
rows.anchor: المعنى واذكر (إذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min ẓuhūrihim is appositional to min banī Ādam; the phrase means God took all their descendants.
rows.anchor: (من ظهورهم) بدل من قوله: (من بني آدم)

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says God created people as tiny particles from Adam's loins and made them testify to His oneness.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم: خلق الله الناس كالذر من صلب آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This could mean that God gave beings like particles the understanding needed to grasp His command, as in the ant's speech and the mountains' praise.
rows.anchor: وهذا جائز أن يكون جعل لأمثال الذر فهما تعقل به أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every child is born with monotheism in the heart, until the parents make the child Jewish or Christian.
rows.anchor: وكل مولود يولد على الفطرة معناه أنه يولد وفي قلبه توحيد الله

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view takes the verse to mean that God brought Adam's descendants out of one another's backs.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: معناه أن الله جل ثناؤه

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: On this view, every adult knows God is one because creation proves His oneness; otherwise disbelievers would have no proof against them, and God has shown His unity through creation.
rows.anchor: أن كل بالغ يعلم أن الله واحد، لأن كل ما خلق الله تعالى دليل على توحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the person who abandons and turns away from God's signs, God gives the worst example in a dog panting in its lowest state.
rows.anchor: ضرب الله عز وجل: بالتارك لآياته والعادل عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A panting dog cannot secure benefit or ward off harm; it pants whether pursued or left alone, which explains the comparison.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الكلب إذا كان يلهث فهو لا يقدر لنفسه على ضر ولا نفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means: evil is the example of the people who denied God's signs.
rows.anchor: المعنى: ساء مثلا مثل القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are described as unable to see with their eyes or understand with their hearts, like those who do not perceive or reason because they leave the truth.
rows.anchor: وصفهم بأنهم لا يبصرون بعيونهم ولا يعقلون بقلوبهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are more astray than cattle because cattle see benefits and harms, while many people knowingly defy God and advance toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: بل هم أضل). وذلك أن الأنعام تبصر منافعها ومضارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in 2:175 means how steadfast they are in doing the deeds of the people of the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال جل وعز: (فما أصبرهم على النار) أي على عمل أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invoke God only by names He has used of Himself or by which He has described Himself; examples include Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Jawād, al-Raḥīm, and al-Qawī, but not Subḥān, al-Rafīq, or al-Jild.
rows.anchor: لا ينبغي أن يدعوه أحد بما لم يصف نفسه به، أو لم يسم به نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs in heaven, earth, and creation should lead people to infer God's oneness.
rows.anchor: أي ألم يستدلوا بما أنبأهم به من ملكوت السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those postponing repentance should consider that their appointed time may be near and they may die in disbelief.
rows.anchor: أي إن كانوا يسوفون بالتوبة فعسى أن يكون قد اقترب أجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse asks whether they will believe in any discourse after this one, since they rejected what God showed them about His oneness and may die as unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى: أولم ينظروا فيما دلهم الله جل ثناؤه على توحيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' course resembled Pharaoh's people's; these were punished by killing and captivity, while Pharaoh's people were drowned and destroyed.
rows.anchor: معناه عادة هؤلاء في كفرهم كعادة آل فرعون في كفرهم،

rows.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some linguists explain dāb as customary practice.
rows.anchor: كذا قال بعض أهل اللغة، في الدأب أنه العادة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the basic sense of dāb is continuing an action: someone persists in it, keeps at it, and exerts himself.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: وحقيقة الداب إدامة العمل

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: This account carries the sense of custom but states it more clearly.
rows.anchor: وهذا التفسير معنى العادة إلا أن هذا أبين وأكشف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh is accusative as the object of remember: remember when Satan adorned their deeds.
rows.anchor: نصب، المعنى: اذكر إذ زين لهم الشيطان أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis appeared to them in the form of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Jaʿtham of Kināna, promising that no one would overcome them and that he would protect them.
rows.anchor: تمثل لهم إبليس في صورة رجل يقال له سراقة بن مالك بن جعثم من كنانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two armies met and saw each other; when Iblis saw angels descending from heaven, he retreated.
rows.anchor: حتى رأت كل واحدة الأخرى، فبصر إبليس بالملائكة تنزل من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After he was censured for fleeing, Iblis disavowed them, saying he saw what they did not and feared God.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه عنف لهربه، فقال: (إني بريء منكم إني أرى ما لا ترون إني أخاف الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakasa means that he returned in disgrace.
rows.anchor: ومعنى نكص رجع بخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though a disbeliever, Iblis said he feared God because he thought the appointed time of his respite had arrived.
rows.anchor: فالجواب في ذلك أنه ظن الوقت الذي أنظر إليه قد حضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrites signal their question about whether anyone sees them because they do not want to say it openly.
rows.anchor: يقولون ذلك إيماء لأنهم منافقون لا يظهرون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask privately and cautiously lest God know what they are doing, although He already knows.
rows.anchor: يقولون ذلك استسرارا وتحذرا من أن يعلم بهم الله - عز وجل -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their turning away may mean leaving the place where they were entitled to remain, or refusing to act on what they heard.
rows.anchor: فجائز أن يكون ينصرفون عن المكان الذي استحقوا فيه، وجائز أن يكون ينصرفون عن العمل بشيء مما يستمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God turned their hearts astray as requital for their conduct.
rows.anchor: أي أضلهم الله مجازاة على فعلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger is a human like them, strengthening the proof because they can understand someone like themselves.
rows.anchor: أي هو بشر مثلكم. أي فهو أوكد للحجة عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means he is an Arab like them, so they know his manner and can understand him.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون عنى به إنه عربي كما أنكم عرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is hard for him when they suffer; ʿanat means encountering hardship.
rows.anchor: أي عزيز عليه عنتكم، والعنت لقاء الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is eager for their faith.
rows.anchor: أي حريص على إيمانكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥasbiya Allāh means that God is sufficient for me.
rows.anchor: أي الذي يكفيني الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zajjaj says two analyses of al-ʿaẓīm here are allowable, without specifying them in this passage.
rows.anchor: رب العرش العظيم). والعظيم ههنا جائزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Daʿwāhum means their supplication: the people of Paradise praise and glorify God in their prayer.
rows.anchor: دعاؤهم، يعني إن دعاء أهل الجنة تنزيه الله وتعظيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their greeting of peace may be what they say to one another or God's greeting of them.
rows.anchor: جائز أن يكون ما يحيي به بعضهم بعضا سلام، وجائز أن يكون الله يحييهم منها بالسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says they begin by glorifying Him, Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: أعلم الله أنهم يبتدئون بتعظيم الله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With lightened an, the phrase omits the heavy anna and its pronoun, meaning that praise belongs to God.
rows.anchor: على حذف أن الشديدة والهاء، والمعنى أنه الحمد لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: يروى
rows.claim: A report says that if people's prayers against themselves, their children, and loved ones were answered, such as May God kill you, they would be destroyed.
rows.anchor: كقول الرجل لابنه وحميمه: أماتك الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse refers to requests such as sending stones from heaven; if God hastened such punishment as He hastens good, it would destroy them.
rows.anchor: وجائز أن يكون عنى قوله: (فأمطر علينا حجارة من السماء)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative istiʿjālahum is like their hastening for good and modifies an omitted verbal noun.
rows.anchor: على مثل استعجالهم بالخير، أي على نعت مصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning is that God would hasten evil with a hastening like their haste for good.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: ولو يعجل الله للناس الشر تعجيلا مثل استعجالهم بالخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both readings, passive la-quḍiya and active la-qaḍā, are sound; Zajjaj prefers the passive reading.
rows.anchor: ويقرأ: لقضي إليهم أجلهم جميعا، جيدتان، ولقضي أحسنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fulk means ship and has the same form in singular and plural, like other Arabic nouns that share one form across number.
rows.anchor: الفلك السفينة، والفلك يكون واحدا ويكون جمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fulka refers to anything round or rounded in shape.
rows.anchor: والفلكة يقال لكل شيء مستدير أو في استدارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By Our eyes and revelation means under Our sight and protection, and according to what We revealed to you.
rows.anchor: أي بإبصارنا إليك وحفظنا لك، وبما أوحينا إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is told not to ask that the disbelievers be given respite, because they will be drowned.
rows.anchor: المعنى: لا تخاطبني في إمهال الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: The people mocked Noah, saying that a man who claimed to be a sent prophet had become a carpenter.
rows.anchor: يقال في التفسير إنهم كانوا يقولون: هذا الذي يزعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah replies that they will regard the mockers as ignorant just as the mockers regard them as ignorant.
rows.anchor: أي نحن نستجهلكم كما تستجهلوننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will learn who is more deserving of disgrace and who has the better outcome.
rows.anchor: أي فسوف تعلمون من هو أحق بالخري، ومن هو أحمد عاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Noah that the time of the people's destruction would be when the oven boiled over.
rows.anchor: نوحا أن وقت إهلاكهم فور التنور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reported explanations identify the tannūr as the earth's surface, the area by the Kufa mosque, a baker's oven, or daybreak.
rows.anchor: وقيل في التنور أقوال. قيل إن التنور وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flood water came from the sky and burst from the earth, as 54:11–12 state; any reported place or time for the oven can serve as the sign of destruction.
rows.anchor: أو في وقت الصبح لا يمنع أن يكون ذلك العلامة لإهلاك القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means from every kind; zawj may refer to one item or one together with its mate, and a pair may mean a male and female bird.
rows.anchor: والزوج في كلام العرب واحد ويجوز أن يكون معه واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading min kulli zawjayni as an annexation or without annexation leaves the meaning unchanged.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ من كل زوجين - على الإضافة - والمعنى واحد في الزوجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wa-ahlaka except whom the decree overtook means carry those who believed.
rows.anchor: أي واحمل من آمن

rows.speaker: يقال
rows.claim: It is said that eighty people believed with Noah.
rows.anchor: ويقال إن الذين آمنوا معه كانوا ثمانين نفسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eighty counts as few relative to Noah's nation.
rows.anchor: لأن ثمانمين قليل في جملة أمة قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By God's name means that the ship runs through God and settles through Him.
rows.anchor: أي بالله تجري، وبه تستقر. ومعنى قلنا باسم الله أي بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings include majrāhā with open mīm and marsāhā with ḍamma, both with ḍamma, and other forms; all are correct and good.
rows.anchor: قرئت مجراها بفتح الميم، ومرساها بضم الميم. وقرئت مجراها ومرساها بضم الميمين جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With open mīm, majrāhā means its running and marsāhā its mooring: by God it is brought to rest.
rows.anchor: فأما من قرأ مجراها بفتح الميم، فالمعنى جريها ومرساها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With both mīms in ḍamma, the phrase means that God causes it to run and to moor; ajraytuhu and ijrāʾ are synonymous.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ مجراها ومرساها. فمعنى ذلك بالله إجراؤها وبالله إرساؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms may also be understood as the verbal nouns from jarat tajrī and rasat tarsū; al-marsā is its place of rest.
rows.anchor: ومن قال مجراها ومرساها، فهو على جرت جريا ومجرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to invoke God's name when the ship is sailing and when it settles; marsāhā is in the genitive as an attribute of God.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أن الله جل وعز أمرهم أن يسموا في وقت جريها ووقت استقرارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unrecited form mujrihā should not be read because recitation is transmitted practice, though it admits a circumstantial parse meaning one who runs and moors it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز فيه شيء لم يقرأ به ولا ينبغي أن يقرأ به لأن القراءة سنة متبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that unrecited form, mujrihā may be an accusative of praise.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا على المدح، أعني مجريها ومرسيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mujrihā and mursīhā may be nominative with an omitted huwa.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مجريها ومرسيها في موضع رفع على إضمار هو مجريها ومرسيها
